name: Square
summary: An omnichannel payments and commerce platform spanning online checkout, invoices, subscriptions, APIs, point of sale, and hardware.

pricing.headline: US online payments are 2.9% + $0.30; country, channel, subscription, and international rates vary.
pricing.assumptions: US online card. Internationally issued cards add 1.5% in the US and other documented markets. Square processing is available only in selected seller countries.

sellerCoverage: Payment processing is supported in selected countries including the US, Canada, Australia, Japan, the UK, Ireland, France, and Spain.
buyerCoverage: Buyers can use supported cards and methods, but Square processes in the seller's supported market and currency rules.
products: Eligible online, service, retail, restaurant, creator, appointment, and subscription businesses.

features.checkout: Online Checkout, Web Payments SDK, hosted links, APIs, and in-person point of sale.
features.subscriptions: Subscriptions API and seller-facing recurring payment tools.
features.invoicing: Square Invoices with market-specific processing rates.
features.paymentMethods: Cards, wallets, Cash App Pay in the US, ACH in the US, and selected BNPL methods.
features.payouts: Standard and eligible instant transfers to the seller's bank account.

responsibilities.note: The Square seller remains the merchant.
Square tools do not generally make Square the legal seller.
Square provides controls and dispute workflows; the seller owns product and transaction risk.
The seller supports fulfillment and buyers.

strengths: Invoices, links, subscriptions, and POS in one ecosystem
limitations: Far fewer seller countries than global-first processors
Less specialized for complex SaaS billing
bestFor: Creators selling online and in person
avoidIf: You need sophisticated global SaaS billing or an MoR
